subject: Logic
title: Negation and Its Tricks
description: A short lesson to help you apply Negation and Its Tricks.

hook.text: Negating "All cats are black" isn't "No cats are black." Getting negation wrong is a classic mistake.

buildup.text: NOT (¬) simply flips truth to false and false to true. ¬P is the opposite of P.

discovery.text: The negation of "all" is "at least one is not." Not "none." This trips up even experienced thinkers.

twist.text: Double negation—¬¬P—brings you back to P. Two flips restore the original truth value.

climax.text: Mastering negation prevents the most common errors in formal reasoning and everyday arguments.

punchline.text: Flip once carefully. Flip twice, you're back.

quiz.question: What is the negation of 'All birds can fly'?
options: At least one bird cannot fly
